VIDEO.title: The Church Won’t Save You
VIDEO.series: The Book of Romans, Every Word (playlist of 28 videos)

kicker: Study aid · Romans 8:1-17 · Episode 13 (#13 of 28 in the playlist)
SUMMARY: The teacher reads Romans 8:1-17. 'There is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus,' for the law of the Spirit of life has set you free from the law of sin and of death (8:1-2). What the Law could not do, weak through the flesh, God did by sending His Son, so that the righteous requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in those who walk according to the Spirit (8:3-4). The mind set on the flesh is death; the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace (8:5-8). The Spirit who raised Jesus dwells in you (8:9-11). Those led by the Spirit are sons of God, who cry 'Abba! Father!', heirs with Christ if we suffer with Him (8:12-17).

The occasion: a church divided over Jewish and Gentile identity, with Torah in the middle. Paul insists the problem was never Torah but sin and death, which hijacked it. Jesus came 'to fulfill' the Law (Matthew 5:17): some commands are fulfilled in His person and work, others lived out by the Spirit. Not all 613 commands bind everyone; the sacrifices ended with Christ (Hebrews 10) and the temple fell in AD 70. Isaiah 2:2-3 pictured the nations coming to learn God's ways without becoming Jews.

Romans 8 is 'not anti-Torah, but pro-Holy Spirit.' Verse 2 connects to verse 4: the law of the Spirit of life frees a person to fulfill the Law's righteous requirement. Walking by the Spirit includes reading and obeying Scripture, which the Spirit carried along (2 Peter 1:21; 2 Timothy 3:16). The 'you' of 8:1-17 is plural except in verse 2: the Spirit indwells a community (John 17).

Across Romans 6-8 Paul retraces the Exodus: passing through the waters (Exodus 14), a change of masters (Exodus 7:16), the Law exposing sin at the golden calf (Exodus 32), wilderness failure (Numbers 11-21), God's presence filling the tabernacle (Exodus 40) and the Spirit giving life to dry bones (Ezekiel 37), the cloud and fire leading (Numbers 9), God as Father (Exodus 4:22; Deuteronomy 32:6; Isaiah 63:16) and inheritance. The new Exodus has arrived in Christ.

Paul mentions the law about 50 times by the video's count. With Dwight Pryor, the teacher holds Paul means the same Torah in different relational contexts: 'Torah plus flesh equals death ... Torah plus Holy Spirit equals life.' Ezekiel 36:26-27 promised a new heart and God's Spirit to walk in His statutes. The lesson: 'The law cannot save anyone or make them righteous. Righteousness is received by faith, and the Holy Spirit then forms believers into the kind of people the law always described.'

Romans 8:5-7 is often used for total depravity and unconditional election; the teacher does not reject those positions but thinks Paul is focused on those who try to obey Torah without the Spirit. Many who attend church speak the language and keep the rituals yet are inwardly untouched by the Spirit, 'cultural Christians.' Life flows only from participation in Christ through the Spirit.
QUOTES: Romans chapter 8 here, it's not anti-Torah, but pro-Holy Spirit.
Torah plus flesh equals death. Not because Torah's bad, but because sin hijacks it. And Torah plus Holy Spirit equals life.
The law cannot save anyone or make them righteous. Righteousness is received by faith. And the Holy Spirit then forms believers into the kind of people the law always described.
The promise was never the removal of Torah, but the renewal of the heart.

method.p: Read Romans 8:1-17 and mark every 'Spirit' and every 'flesh.' Beside each 'Spirit,' write what the Spirit does (frees, dwells, gives life, leads, testifies). Then list the Exodus pictures you can hear behind each one.

src.text: Therefore there is now no condemnation for those who are in Christ Jesus. For the law of the Spirit of life in Christ Jesus has set you free from the law of sin and of death.

lines.text: Having concluded his larger argument, Paul turns to the indwelling Holy Spirit, who has set the church free and gives life to those whose minds are set on Him.
Verse 2 connects to verse 4: the law of the Spirit of life frees a person to fulfill the righteous requirement of the Law. In 8:1-17 every 'you' is plural except in verse 2.

FREE.title: What the Law could not do

left.text: For what the Law could not do, weak as it was through the flesh, God did: sending His own Son in the likeness of sinful flesh and as an offering for sin, He condemned sin in the flesh, so that the righteous requirement of the Law might be fulfilled in us, who do not walk according to the flesh but according to the Spirit.

right.text: “Do not think that I came to abolish the Law or the Prophets; I did not come to abolish but to fulfill.

lines.text: The Law was never designed to make anyone righteous, because of indwelling sin (Paul's point in Romans 7). Jesus is not a prophet reinterpreting an old text but the God-man who embodies its commands. Torah reaches its goal in Him.
Not all 613 commands bind everyone: many concern ritual purity Christ alone fulfills, and after AD 70 the sacrifices could not be offered; Christ ended them (Hebrews 10:12).

src.text: And many peoples will come and say, / “Come, let us go up to the mountain of Yahweh, / To the house of the God of Jacob, / That He may instruct us from His ways / And that we may walk in His paths.” / For from Zion the law will go forth / And the word of Yahweh from Jerusalem.

lines.text: The boundary markers that made an ethnic distinction between Jew and non-Jew are not required of Gentile-background Christians. The promise of every nation worshiping at Zion never required everyone to become a Jew, only to worship together and learn God's ways.
Believers stay connected to Torah 'not through Sinai obligation, but through Spirit-empowered conformity to Jesus Christ.'

left.text: So the sons of Israel went through the midst of the sea on the dry land, and the waters were a wall to them on their right hand and on their left.

right.text: Then the people saw that Moses delayed to come down from the mountain. So the people assembled about Aaron and said to him, “Arise, make us gods who will go before us; as for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.”

lines.text: Romans 6: buried and raised through baptism (the Red Sea), and a change of masters ('Let My people go, that they may serve Me,' Exodus 7:16). Romans 7: the Law reveals sin, as the golden calf was made while Moses received the Law.
Then the Law without the promised heart renewal (Isaiah 29:13; Jeremiah 9:25-26) and wilderness frustration, willing but failing (Numbers 11-21).

left.text: Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle.

right.text: Now whenever the cloud would go up from over the tent, afterward the sons of Israel would then set out; and in the place where the cloud settled down, there the sons of Israel would camp.

lines.text: The Spirit 'dwells in you' (plural), as God's glory filled the tabernacle among His people. 'Being led by the Spirit' (8:14) recalls the pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.
'The law of the Spirit of life' (8:2) echoes Ezekiel 37: 'I will put My Spirit within you, and you will come to life' (Ezekiel 37:14).

left.text: Then you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “Israel is My son, My firstborn.

right.text: For you have not received a spirit of slavery leading to fear again, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons by whom we cry out, “Abba! Father!”

lines.text: God is Father to His people in Exodus 4, Deuteronomy 32 and Isaiah 63: 'You, O Yahweh, are our Father' (Isaiah 63:16). Israel's inheritance of the land (Genesis 12; Deuteronomy 8) widens to the renewed creation.
Obedience and assurance flow not from effort, ethnicity or possession of Torah but from the indwelling Spirit. The long-awaited new Exodus has arrived in Christ.

src.text: For the mind set on the flesh is death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace, because the mind set on the flesh is at enmity toward God, for it does not subject itself to the law of God, for it is not even able to do so,

lines.text: This works out Romans 7:5: passions aroused by the Law bear fruit for death and do not and cannot submit to God's law. Note the reference to Torah at the end of 8:7.

Often used to argue total depravity and unconditional election; the teacher does not say those positions are wrong, but thinks Paul is focused on unregenerate Jews and God-fearers trying to obey Torah within a covenant context.

MIND.title: A new heart and My Spirit

src.text: Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will be careful to do My judgments.

lines.text: Paul is not saying 'become Torah-observant Jews' but 'walk by the Spirit and the righteous intent of Torah will be fulfilled in you.' Christians cannot reject the word of God in the name of rejecting works of the law; the problem was the human heart.
With Dwight Pryor, the teacher holds that Paul always means the same Torah, in different relational contexts: with the flesh, the law of sin and death; with the Spirit, the law of the Spirit of life.

src.text: However, you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Him.

lines.text: Many speak the Christian language fluently, keep Christian rituals and identify as Christian socially or politically, yet remain inwardly untouched by the Spirit: what Richard Dawkins calls cultural Christians, living an external religious life.
Paul's point is not to shame but to show that obedience, assurance and life flow only from participation in Christ through the Spirit, not from religious identity alone.

BACKGROUND.p: Roman adoption (adoptio) transferred a person, often an adult, into a new family with full rights of a natural son, including inheritance; old debts and obligations were cancelled. Paul's Roman readers knew this well, and Paul also draws on Israel's sonship (Romans 9:4).
Rabbinic tradition (Talmud, Makkot 23b) counts 613 commandments in the Torah: 248 positive and 365 negative. Many concern the priesthood, temple and sacrifices, which could not be kept after AD 70.

BACKGROUND.h: The Spirit in the Old Testament
BACKGROUND.p: The prophets promised a future outpouring of God's Spirit on all His people (Ezekiel 36:27; 37:14; Joel 2:28-29). The early church saw it fulfilled at Pentecost (Acts 2:16-18).

DEBATES.h: What is 'the law of the Spirit of life'? (8:2)
DEBATES.p: Some read 'law' here as a principle or power (the Spirit's rule versus sin's rule). Others, like the video and Dwight Pryor, read it as the Mosaic Law itself, now working through the Spirit. Chrysostom took it as the Spirit Himself.

Reformed interpreters often cite 8:7-8 for human inability apart from grace. Others read it more narrowly as Paul's description of life under the Law in the flesh. The video takes the narrower focus without denying the doctrine.

DEBATES.h: Who are the 'sons of God' in 8:14?
DEBATES.p: Most see all believers, Jew and Gentile, now sharing Israel's title (Exodus 4:22). Some stress Roman adoption; others the new Exodus. Many combine the two.

CAREFUL_INTRO: Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
CAREFUL: The video cites Jeremiah 9:12 for Israel 'uncircumcised of heart'; the phrase is in Jeremiah 9:26.

By the LSB's own word tags, 'law' (Greek nomos) appears about 68 times from Romans 1:1 to 8:17 (chapter 2: 19, 3: 11, 4: 5, 5: 3, 6: 2, 7: 23, 8:1-17: 5); the video's tally is lower, but its point about Paul's many uses stands.
The captions spell the scholars 'Dwight Prior' and 'Lois Teverberg'; the names are Dwight Pryor and Lois Tverberg.
The video reads 'debtors' in 8:12 and 'deeds of the body' in 8:13; the LSB has 'under obligation' and 'practices of the body.'

QUESTIONS: What difference does 'no condemnation' make to how you face your sin today?
Which Exodus picture behind Romans 8 helps you most: waters, presence, cloud, Father or inheritance?
How does reading the 'you' of Romans 8 as plural change how you think about the Spirit's work?
Where could your faith slide into external religious life?
What does it look like for your day to be led by the Spirit rather than plowed through?
APPLICATION_VIDEO: In every age some people inhabit Christian culture, affirm Christian values and even pursue moral obedience without the regenerating work of the Holy Spirit. The teacher, a Southern Baptist pastor whose study of the Jewishness of Jesus began in 2018 and has, he says, reinforced rather than overturned traditional teaching, admits that someone with two channels and a full-time ministry can slip into external religious life. When he says yes to too much, a whole day goes by without prayer, without asking God to guide or examine him. Everything a Christian does must flow from the overflow of the inward relationship with God through the indwelling Spirit.
APPLICATION_ADDED: Study note (added): tomorrow morning, before your first task, pray Romans 8:14-16 and ask the Spirit to lead your day. At day's end, note one moment you were led and one you plowed through.

So the people assembled about Aaron and said to him, “Arise, make us gods who will go before us; as for this Moses, the man who brought us up from the land of Egypt, we do not know what has become of him.”"

   (video) Then the Law without the promised heart renewal (Isaiah 29:13; Jeremiah 9:25-26) and wilderness frustration, willing but failing (Numbers 11-21). (Isaiah 29:13; Jeremiah 9:25-26)
2. Exodus 40:34; Numbers 9:17: Presence and guidance
   Exodus (Exodus 40:34, LSB): "Then the cloud covered the tent of meeting, and the glory of Yahweh filled the tabernacle."
   Numbers (Numbers 9:17, LSB): "Now whenever the cloud would go up from over the tent, afterward the sons of Israel would then set out; and in the place where the cloud settled down, there the sons of Israel would camp."
   (video) The Spirit 'dwells in you' (plural), as God's glory filled the tabernacle among His people. 'Being led by the Spirit' (8:14) recalls the pillar of cloud by day and fire by night.
   (video) 'The law of the Spirit of life' (8:2) echoes Ezekiel 37: 'I will put My Spirit within you, and you will come to life' (Ezekiel 37:14). (Ezekiel 37:14)
3. Exodus 4:22; Romans 8:15-17: Sons, Father and heirs
   Yahweh to Moses (Exodus 4:22, LSB): "Then you shall say to Pharaoh, ‘Thus says Yahweh, “Israel is My son, My firstborn."
   Paul (Romans 8:15, LSB): "For you have not received a spirit of slavery leading to fear again, but you have received the Spirit of adoption as sons by whom we cry out, “Abba! Father!”"
   (video) God is Father to His people in Exodus 4, Deuteronomy 32 and Isaiah 63: 'You, O Yahweh, are our Father' (Isaiah 63:16). Israel's inheritance of the land (Genesis 12; Deuteronomy 8) widens to the renewed creation. (Isaiah 63:16; Deuteronomy 32:6)
   (video) Obedience and assurance flow not from effort, ethnicity or possession of Torah but from the indwelling Spirit. The long-awaited new Exodus has arrived in Christ.

## Two mindsets
1. Romans 8:5-8: Two mindsets
   Death or life and peace Romans 8:6-7: "For the mind set on the flesh is death, but the mind set on the Spirit is life and peace, because the mind set on the flesh is at enmity toward God, for it does not subject itself to the law of God, for it is not even able to do so," https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+8:6-7
   (video) This works out Romans 7:5: passions aroused by the Law bear fruit for death and do not and cannot submit to God's law. Note the reference to Torah at the end of 8:7. (Romans 7:5)
   (video) Often used to argue total depravity and unconditional election; the teacher does not say those positions are wrong, but thinks Paul is focused on unregenerate Jews and God-fearers trying to obey Torah within a covenant context.
2. Ezekiel 36:26-27: A new heart and My Spirit
   Renewal, not removal Ezekiel 36:26-27: "Moreover, I will give you a new heart and put a new spirit within you; and I will remove the heart of stone from your flesh and give you a heart of flesh. I will put My Spirit within you and cause you to walk in My statutes, and you will be careful to do My judgments." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Ezekiel+36:26-27
   (video) Paul is not saying 'become Torah-observant Jews' but 'walk by the Spirit and the righteous intent of Torah will be fulfilled in you.' Christians cannot reject the word of God in the name of rejecting works of the law; the problem was the human heart.
   (video) With Dwight Pryor, the teacher holds that Paul always means the same Torah, in different relational contexts: with the flesh, the law of sin and death; with the Spirit, the law of the Spirit of life.
3. Romans 8:9-11: Inside, not only outside
   Not cultural Christianity Romans 8:9: "However, you are not in the flesh but in the Spirit, if indeed the Spirit of God dwells in you. But if anyone does not have the Spirit of Christ, he does not belong to Him." https://read.lsbible.org/?q=Romans+8:9
   (video) Many speak the Christian language fluently, keep Christian rituals and identify as Christian socially or politically, yet remain inwardly untouched by the Spirit: what Richard Dawkins calls cultural Christians, living an external religious life.
   (video) Paul's point is not to shame but to show that obedience, assurance and life flow only from participation in Christ through the Spirit, not from religious identity alone.

## Key people
- Paul: Turns to the indwelling Spirit after his long argument about Torah, sin and death. [Background] Writing to a mixed Jewish and Gentile church in Rome.
- Jesus: Came not to abolish the Law but to fulfill it (Matthew 5:17); the God-man who embodies its commands. [Background] Sent 'in the likeness of sinful flesh' (Romans 8:3).
- Moses: Received the Law while the people made the golden calf (Exodus 32). [Background] The cloud filled the tabernacle he set up (Exodus 40:34-35).
- Ezekiel: Promised a new heart and God's Spirit within (36:26-27); saw dry bones live (37). [Background] Prophet among the exiles in Babylon.
- Dwight Pryor: The teacher agrees with him that Paul speaks of the same Torah in different relational contexts. [Background] American Bible teacher (d. 2011) known for studies of the Jewish background of Jesus.
- Richard Dawkins: His phrase 'cultural Christians' names people who identify as Christian without the Spirit's renewal. [Background] British biologist and outspoken atheist who has described himself as a cultural Christian.

## Places [Background]
- Red Sea crossing (named in the video): Israel passed through the waters (Exodus 14); the video hears baptism in Romans 6. Location debated; pin at the Gulf of Suez.
- Mount Sinai (named in the video): The golden calf was made while Moses received the Law (Exodus 32). Traditional site.
- Wilderness of Paran: Where the cloud led Israel and the wilderness failures unfolded (Numbers 10:12).
- Jerusalem (Zion) (named in the video): 'From Zion the law will go forth' (Isaiah 2:3).
- Rome (named in the video): A church divided over Jewish and Gentile identity.

## Key terms
- Condemnation: The judicial sentence against sin; none remains for those in Christ (Romans 8:1).
- Law of the Spirit of life: In the video: Torah as it operates with the Spirit, producing life; contrast 'the law of sin and of death' (8:2).
- Righteous requirement: What the Law rightly requires, fulfilled in those who walk by the Spirit (8:4).
- Mind set on the flesh: A way of thinking oriented to the flesh; it is death and enmity toward God (8:6-7).
- Adoption as sons: Being made God's children and heirs by the Spirit (8:15).
- Abba: Aramaic for 'father,' used by Jesus (Mark 14:36) and by believers through the Spirit. [Background]
- Tanakh: The Hebrew Bible: Torah, Prophets and Writings.
- Cultural Christian: Someone who identifies with Christian culture without the Spirit's inward renewal.

## Historical and cultural background [Background: established]
- Adoption in Roman law: Roman adoption (adoptio) transferred a person, often an adult, into a new family with full rights of a natural son, including inheritance; old debts and obligations were cancelled. Paul's Roman readers knew this well, and Paul also draws on Israel's sonship (Romans 9:4).
- 613 commandments: Rabbinic tradition (Talmud, Makkot 23b) counts 613 commandments in the Torah: 248 positive and 365 negative. Many concern the priesthood, temple and sacrifices, which could not be kept after AD 70.
- The Spirit in the Old Testament: The prophets promised a future outpouring of God's Spirit on all His people (Ezekiel 36:27; 37:14; Joel 2:28-29). The early church saw it fulfilled at Pentecost (Acts 2:16-18).

## Early witnesses [Background: sourced]
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 391): "The other was merely given by the Spirit, but this even furnishes those that receive it with the Spirit in large measure." Homilies on Romans 13, on 8:2. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 391): "For he does not speak of the badness of the Law, but of what it could not do; and so again, in that it was weak, not, in that it was mischievous, or designing." Homilies on Romans 13, on 8:3. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).
- John Chrysostom (c. AD 391): "For it is not from the language merely, he says, that I make my assertion, but from the cause out of which the language has its birth; since it is from the Spirit suggesting it that we so speak." Homilies on Romans 14, on 8:16. NPNF 1.11 (public domain).

## Where scholars differ [Background: debated]
- What is 'the law of the Spirit of life'? (8:2) Some read 'law' here as a principle or power (the Spirit's rule versus sin's rule). Others, like the video and Dwight Pryor, read it as the Mosaic Law itself, now working through the Spirit. Chrysostom took it as the Spirit Himself.
- Does Romans 8:5-8 teach total depravity? Reformed interpreters often cite 8:7-8 for human inability apart from grace. Others read it more narrowly as Paul's description of life under the Law in the flesh. The video takes the narrower focus without denying the doctrine.
- Who are the 'sons of God' in 8:14? Most see all believers, Jew and Gentile, now sharing Israel's title (Exodus 4:22). Some stress Roman adoption; others the new Exodus. Many combine the two.

## Careful reading notes
Small slips worth knowing (offered gently; the video's main points stand):
- The video cites Jeremiah 9:12 for Israel 'uncircumcised of heart'; the phrase is in Jeremiah 9:26.
- By the LSB's own word tags, 'law' (Greek nomos) appears about 68 times from Romans 1:1 to 8:17 (chapter 2: 19, 3: 11, 4: 5, 5: 3, 6: 2, 7: 23, 8:1-17: 5); the video's tally is lower, but its point about Paul's many uses stands.
- The captions spell the scholars 'Dwight Prior' and 'Lois Teverberg'; the names are Dwight Pryor and Lois Tverberg.
- The video reads 'debtors' in 8:12 and 'deeds of the body' in 8:13; the LSB has 'under obligation' and 'practices of the body.'

## Reflection and discussion questions
1. What difference does 'no condemnation' make to how you face your sin today?
2. Which Exodus picture behind Romans 8 helps you most: waters, presence, cloud, Father or inheritance?
3. How does reading the 'you' of Romans 8 as plural change how you think about the Spirit's work?
4. Where could your faith slide into external religious life?
5. What does it look like for your day to be led by the Spirit rather than plowed through?

## Application
- (video) In every age some people inhabit Christian culture, affirm Christian values and even pursue moral obedience without the regenerating work of the Holy Spirit. The teacher, a Southern Baptist pastor whose study of the Jewishness of Jesus began in 2018 and has, he says, reinforced rather than overturned traditional teaching, admits that someone with two channels and a full-time ministry can slip into external religious life. When he says yes to too much, a whole day goes by without prayer, without asking God to guide or examine him. Everything a Christian does must flow from the overflow of the inward relationship with God through the indwelling Spirit.
- Study note (added): tomorrow morning, before your first task, pray Romans 8:14-16 and ask the Spirit to lead your day. At day's end, note one moment you were led and one you plowed through.
